notesStmt.note: A note in Whitman's hand at the top of this manuscript reads "Camden New Jersey / Oct 17 '84." The corrections were likely made around that time.
A corrected proof slip of the poem "Of That Blithe Throat of Thine," which was first published in Harper's Monthly Magazine in January 1885. The poem was later included in November Boughs (1888).

epigraph.p: [More than 83 degrees north—about a good days' steaming distance to the Pole by one of our fast oceaners in clear water—Greely heard the song of a single snow-bird merrily sounding over the desolation.]

lg.l: Of that blithe throat of thine from arctic bleak and blank,

I'll mind the lesson, solitary bird—let me too welcome chilliun/g

Old age land-lock'd within its winter bay—(cold.,/ cold, O cold!)

For them thy faith‸,/ thy rule I take, and grave it to the last;

Not summer's zones alone—not chants of youth or south's warm

These with gay heart I also sing.
